newsitem.title: CHINA: HK stocks to drift sideways, watch interbank rates.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks to drift sideways, watch interbank rates.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks are expected to drift sideways on Monday with investors taking a wait-and-see attitude amid Asian currency concerns, brokers said.
"The market is lacking direction and the focus is on short-term interest rates," said Antony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas.
Overnight rates rose above six percent on tight liquidity in the midst of currency jitters in Asian markets, brokers said.
"This will keep the Hang Seng index from moving in a big way either way," Mak said, adding that the blue-chip index was likely to keep within a 100-point range on Monday.
On Friday, the Hang Seng Index lost 51.11 points, or 0.33 percent, to 15,658.12. The Hang Seng London Reference Index eased 58.40 points, or 0.37 percent, to 15,599.72.

"Individual stocks such as banks, properties and those with rumours of being a purchase target of Chinese companies and H-shares with restructuring concept should continue to attract buyers," said Charles Cheung, executive director at J & A Securities.
He said the market was expected to be sluggish with upward potential.
